messages:
Arjun: quick heads-up — while bringing up HF model `big-palm-v1` (quantized) I noticed sampling behavior drift after our hf->redwood generation_config conversion. samples are much more repetitive.
Maya: ugh. repro steps?
Arjun: minimal. load HF `generation_config.json` from the model card, run our converter, then call /v1/generate with the mapped params. HF cfg has `repetition_penalty: 1.1`, `do_sample: true`, `top_k: 50`, `top_p: 0.95`, `temperature: 0.8`.
Arjun: converter output for this model looks like:
```
{"temperature": "0.8", "top_p": "0.95", "top_k": "50", "repetition_penalty": "1.0"}
```
Arjun: note repetition_penalty went to 1.0 — that's the bug I think. our fallback overwrote it.
Eli: why would fallback do that? do we coerce types somewhere (e.g., string->float) and treat missing/NaN as default=1? :thinking: 
Maya: I dug in — code path is convert_generation_config() in onboarding service. We call get_safe(cfg, "repetition_penalty", default=1.0) AFTER applying quantization-normalizations. For quantized models we run a `sampling_safety()` pass that currently clamps rep_penalty <= 1.0 if model is int8 because of a heuristic from 2023.
Sophia: clamping rep_penalty for int8 models seems dangerous — it directly undoes author intent. Did we add a flag anywhere to opt-out? :facepalm: 
Maya: no flag. I think this was trying to prevent token collapse in older kernels but it's too coarse.
Eli: aside from rep_penalty, we also need to watch `do_sample` semantics. HF `do_sample=false` -> greedy. Our current mapping turns that into `top_k: 0` and `temperature: 1.0` which is wrong. Greedy should map to `temperature: 0` (or top_k:1). We have two incompatible conventions floating around.
Arjun: yes. example: HF gen config
```
{
 "do_sample": false, "temperature": 1.0, "top_k": 0
}
```
Arjun: should map to Redwood
```
{
 "do_sample": false, "temperature": "0.0", "top_k": "1"
}
```
Maya: we also had confusion for top_k=0 meaning "no top_k" vs some libs meaning greedy. need canonicalization.
Sophia: extra gotcha — chat templates. HF chat templates sometimes include special tokens as separate entries in generation_config or tokenizer.special_tokens_map. Example: assistant_start = "<|assistant|>" and eos="</s>". Our conversion sometimes strips those into prompt text and we end up duplicating tokens: generated chat includes extra assistant markers and sampling sees a shifted distribution.
Eli: concrete symptom: after conversion prompts end with assistant token, then model sampling receives that token as last token and our prefix-caching returns a shorter kv cache, causing temperature interpretation oddity.
Arjun: reproduction snippet I used:
```
# HF generation_config.json
{
 "temperature": 0.8,
 "top_p": 0.95,
 "top_k": 50,
 "repetition_penalty": 1.1,
 "do_sample": true
}
# Redwood mapped params (broken)
{"temperature":"0.8","top_p":"0.95","top_k":"50","repetition_penalty":"1.0"}
```
Maya: TL;DR: two issues — (1) rep_penalty clamped for quantized models, (2) do_sample/top_k/temperature canonicalization is inconsistent with HF semantics. Also (3) chat template special tokens sometimes mishandled.
Sophia: proposed fixes:
- remove the aggressive clamp for repetition_penalty; instead add an opt-in compatibility shim per-model with explicit flag `compat.sampling_clamp: true`.
- canonicalize `do_sample=false` -> `temperature=0` & `top_k=1` in converter.
- ensure tokenizer.special_tokens_map entries are persisted as metadata and not inlined into prompts by template renderer.
Eli: please add unit tests: two conversion cases + a quantized-model regression test that compares top_k/top_p sampling from HF Python vs our runtime with same seeds.
Maya: I'm opening a PR with the clamp removal and tests. will also add a TODO to add opt-in compat flags on model metadata.
Maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2345 :rocket:
deploy-bot: CI started for PR 2345 — 7 jobs
Arjun: awesome. can we also add a quick eval run (20 prompts) comparing logprobs and repetitive ngram counts between HF reference and RW runtime? if we see < 2% divergence it's fine, else revert.
Sophia: yes I'll add the eval harness to the PR and run it on the qa cluster (quantized). putting it on my todo.
Eli: assign me to code review + add a sandbox test that sets repetition_penalty=1.3 and ensures converter preserves it.
Maya: thanks. I'll change the converter and ping y'all when CI green.
Arjun: thanks team. follow-up: add a small doc to devex about canonical mapping rules so future model onboards don't hit this.
